cues.en: This talk comes from a scientific discovery.

cues.en: There were some social scientists who were doing some work, as they do, in trying to

cues.zh: 理解人类智能。
cues.en: understand human intelligence.

cues.zh: 我们是怎么思考的？
cues.en: How do we think?

cues.zh: 我们的大脑是如何运作的？
cues.en: How do our brains work?

cues.zh: 他们设计了一组简单的实验，结果却非常令人惊讶。
cues.en: They came up with a set of simple experiments and their results were really surprising.

cues.zh: 他们发表了结果，科学界说这不可能，
cues.en: They published their results and the scientific community said that can't be right, there

cues.zh: 一定是实验设计有问题，一定是
cues.en: must have been an error in the design of the experiments, there must have been some error

cues.en: in the evaluation of the data.

cues.zh: 这不可能是对我们如何思考的正确解释。
cues.en: This cannot possibly be the correct explanation for how we think.

cues.zh: 但这些结果至少足够有趣，以至于其他人尝试复现
cues.en: But the results were at least interesting enough that other people attempted to replicate

cues.zh: 这些研究，接着又做了后续研究和新的实验。
cues.en: the studies, and then did follow on studies and new experiments.

cues.zh: 结论是：没错，确实如此，我们实际上就是这样思考的。
cues.en: The conclusion was: yeah, it's true, we actually think like this.

cues.zh: 科学大致就是这样运作的：有人会做出一个实验，得出的结论
cues.en: This is sort of how science works, where someone will come up with an experiment which has

cues.zh: 与科学界普遍接受的共识相矛盾，
cues.en: a conclusion which contradicts what is commonly understood by the scientific consensus, and

cues.zh: 于是立刻就会受到质疑。
cues.en: it will immediately be challenged.

cues.zh: 但我们会尝试复现实验。如果结果站得住脚，科学共识
cues.en: But then we'll try to replicate it, and if it bears out then the scientific consensus

cues.zh: 就会随之改变，直到后续实验再次推翻它。
cues.en: changes to adopt that, until further experiments will contradict again.

cues.zh: 然后就会有人获得诺贝尔奖。
cues.en: Then there's a Nobel Prize.

cues.en: All of that happened in this case.

cues.zh: 科学就是这样发展的。
cues.en: This is how science happens.

cues.zh: 这些内容都写在丹尼尔·加德纳的一本好书里：《恐惧的科学》。
cues.en: This is all told in a wonderful book: The Science of Fear by Daniel Gardner.

cues.zh: 加德纳谈到了这项研究及其对社会的影响，也谈到了这样一个事实：
cues.en: Gardner talks about this research and its implications on society, and the fact that

cues.zh: 由于我们的思维方式，我们往往会误解什么才是真正的危险。
cues.en: because of the way we think, we tend to misunderstand what danger is.

cues.zh: 我们害怕的东西往往不对。
cues.en: We fear the wrong things.

cues.zh: 害怕错误的东西，后果反而是让自己陷入更大的
cues.en: The consequence of fearing the wrong things is that you actually put yourself in greater

cues.zh: 危险。
cues.en: danger.

cues.zh: 好书，强烈推荐。
cues.en: Great book, I highly recommend it.

cues.zh: 这个发现究竟是什么，如此惊人、如此不同寻常，而且很可能是真的？
cues.en: What was this discovery that was so amazing and unusual and probably true?

cues.zh: 那就是大脑里有两个系统。
cues.en: It was that there are two systems in the brain.

cues.zh: 系统二可以称为“头脑”。
cues.en: System two could be called the head.

cues.zh: 我们在这里做分析性思考，在这里做算术和数学。
cues.en: It's where we do analytical thinking, it's where we do arithmetic and mathematics.

cues.zh: 我们在这里进行深度思考。
cues.en: It's where we think deep thoughts.

cues.zh: 它很棒，但问题在于它有点慢。
cues.en: It's great, but the problem with it is it's kind of slow.

cues.zh: 正因为头脑有点慢，我们才不得不发明计算机，因为现代
cues.en: It's because the head is kind of slow that we had to invent computers, because the modern

cues.zh: 世界需要大量的数字运算，而我们在这方面并不擅长。
cues.en: world demanded a lot of number crunching, and we're just not very good at that.

cues.zh: 我们需要比我们更快的机器来做这些事。
cues.en: We needed machines that were faster than we were at doing that stuff.

cues.zh: 然后是系统一，可以称为“直觉”。
cues.en: Then there's system one, which could be called the gut.

cues.zh: 它是从战或逃反应演化而来的。
cues.en: It's evolved from the flight or fight response.

cues.zh: 它非常非常快，但快也有代价，所以它会犯错。
cues.en: It is very, very fast, but there are tradeoffs in the way it's fast, so it makes mistakes.

cues.zh: 如果你见过一只猫站在那里，然后突然受惊跑开，
cues.en: If you ever saw a cat just standing there and then suddenly he freaks out and runs,

cues.zh: 接着它停下来，好像在说“我本来就打算这么做”，这就是战或逃反应。
cues.en: and then he stops and goes yeah, I meant to do that, that's the flight or fight response.

cues.zh: 这个系统的偏向是，误报也没关系，因为
cues.en: The biases in that system are set so that false positives are OK, because it's better

cues.zh: 误报总比反应慢要好，不然你就来不及躲开
cues.en: to get a false positive than a slow positive, because then you don't have time to get out

cues.zh: 朝你扑来的东西。
cues.en: of the way of whatever's at you.

cues.zh: 你会看到一群鸟突然莫名其妙地飞起来，然后又飞回来；这就是那种
cues.en: You'll see a flock of birds suddenly take off for no reason and come back; that's that

cues.zh: 机制。
cues.en: mechanism.

cues.zh: 我们有这种机制。
cues.en: We got that.

cues.zh: 直觉反应确实很快，但只是近似的，因为它不懂算术，也不能
cues.en: The gut is really fast, but it's only approximate because it doesn't know arithmetic, it can't

cues.zh: 解决难题。
cues.en: solve hard problems.

cues.zh: 但它并不是在试图解决难题，只是在寻找某几类模式，
cues.en: But it's not trying to solve hard problems, it's just looking for certain kinds of patterns,

cues.zh: 一旦发现这些模式，它就会做出反应。
cues.en: and when it sees those patterns it reacts.

cues.zh: 头脑和直觉本身都不让人意外。
cues.en: Now, neither the head nor the gut are surprising.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，这些我们都知道。
cues.en: I mean, we all know about that.

cues.zh: 我的头脑告诉我一回事，直觉却告诉我另一回事。
cues.en: My head tells me this but my gut tells me that.

cues.zh: 我们总会有这样的体验。
cues.en: We're always experiencing that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 这项研究让人意外的是，这两个系统之间的联系。
cues.en: The surprise in this research was the connection between those two systems.

cues.zh: 事实证明，直觉会影响头脑。
cues.en: It turns out that the gut informs the head.

cues.zh: 直觉会为头脑的运算设定假设。
cues.en: The gut sets up the assumptions that the head is going to use in doing its computation.

cues.zh: 头脑通常并不知道这一点。
cues.en: The head is not generally aware that that's the case.

cues.zh: 直觉告诉头脑的事情，会比头脑自己经历过的事情更受重视，
cues.en: The things that the gut tells the head are weighed as more important than things that

cues.zh: 而头脑本身经历过的事情则没那么受重视。
cues.en: the head itself has experienced.

cues.zh: 所以，只要扰乱人们的直觉，就很容易把他们搞糊涂。
cues.en: That makes it really easy to confuse people by confusing their guts.

cues.zh: 这对科学界来说还是个新闻，但还有另一个群体
cues.en: This was news to the scientific community, but there is another community which has known

cues.zh: 早就知道这回事了，而且知道了很多很多年，那当然就是广告界。
cues.en: about this stuff for a long, long time, and that is of course the advertising community.

cues.zh: 他们几十年前就摸清了这一套；这对他们来说不新鲜，因为他们有很多
cues.en: They figured this stuff out decades ago; this is not news to them, because a lot of their

cues.zh: 生意就是把我们不需要的东西卖给我们。
cues.en: business is selling stuff to us that we don't need.

cues.zh: 他们让我们想要那些其实并不想要的东西。
cues.en: They create wants for things that we don't really want.

cues.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？
cues.en: How do they do that?

cues.zh: 靠跟脑子说话可做不到，他们得跟你的本能说话，而没有谁
cues.en: You don't do that by talking to the head, you do that by talking to the gut, and nobody

cues.zh: 比烟草业更擅长这一套。
cues.en: is better than the tobacco industry.

cues.zh: 看看烟草就知道了。
cues.en: Because look at tobacco.

cues.zh: 烟草会带来什么？
cues.en: What does tobacco do?

cues.zh: 它会让你身上有异味。
cues.en: It makes you smell bad.

cues.zh: 你从点燃第一支烟开始，身上就臭了。
cues.en: From the first time you light up, you stink.

cues.zh: 烟草就是这样。
cues.en: Tobacco does that.

cues.zh: 然后你的牙齿会变黄。
cues.en: Then your teeth turn yellow.

cues.zh: 接着你会生病，然后死去。
cues.en: Then you get sick, and then you die.

cues.zh: 这就是烟草干的事。
cues.en: That's what tobacco does.

cues.zh: 那你怎么推销这种产品？
cues.en: So how do you sell a product like that?

cues.zh: 你不是卖给头脑，你是卖给直觉。
cues.en: You don't sell it to the head, you sell it to the gut.

cues.zh: 如果你问一个烟民“你为什么抽烟？”
cues.en: If you ask a smoker "why do you smoke?"

cues.zh: 嗯，为什么，这是个分析性问题，所以这得靠头脑来回答。
cues.en: Well, why, that's an analytical question, so that goes to the head.

cues.zh: 但头脑现在会开始用从直觉那里得来的事实来思考，而
cues.en: But the head is going to now start thinking with facts that it got from the gut, and the

cues.zh: 直觉说抽烟不危险，因为直觉看待危险的方式不同；
cues.en: gut says cigarette smoking is not dangerous because of the way the gut looks at danger;

cues.zh: 它看的是眼前的危险，它看的是吓人的危险。
cues.en: it's looking at immediate danger, it's looking at shocking danger.

cues.zh: 缓慢的死亡不会被注意到。
cues.en: Slow death doesn't register.

cues.zh: 所以缓慢的死亡就跟对你有好处一样。
cues.en: So slow death is as good as good for you.

cues.zh: 如果你有任何逻辑体系，而你从错误的前提开始，你就能得出错误的
cues.en: If you have any logical system and you start with false premises, you can reach a false

cues.zh: 结论。
cues.en: conclusion.

cues.zh: 我是说，我们知道这一点；逻辑告诉我们的。
cues.en: I mean, we know that; logic tells us that.

cues.zh: 但我们就是这么思考的。
cues.en: But that's how we think.

cues.zh: 你可以问一个烟民“你为什么抽烟？”，你可以和他们一起坐在餐厅里
cues.en: You can ask a smoker "why do you smoke?" and you can be sitting with them in a restaurant

cues.zh: 如果他理性的话，他会说“我抽烟，嗯，那太蠢了，我应该马上戒掉。”
cues.en: and if he were rational he'd go "I smoke, well that's stupid, I should stop immediately."

cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。
cues.en: But that's not what happens.

cues.zh: 相反，他会想：“我为什么抽烟？
cues.en: Instead he's trying to think "why do I smoke?

cues.zh: 肯定有充分的理由。
cues.en: There must be good reasons for it.

cues.zh: 嗯，这让我受欢迎。”
cues.en: Um, it makes me popular."

cues.zh: 他会这么说，却没注意到身边那些健康、好闻的人
cues.en: And he'll say that not noticing that the healthy good smelling people who are near him are

cues.zh: 正试图躲开他，免得他污染自己的食物。
cues.en: trying to get away so he doesn't taint his food.

cues.zh: 所以人们会一直抽烟，直到抽烟要了他们的命，直到他们死去。
cues.en: So people will smoke until it kills them, until they die.

cues.zh: 你可以说这是因为尼古丁成瘾，他们是成瘾者，所以才这样，
cues.en: You could say that's because of nicotine addiction, they're addicts and that's why it happens,

cues.zh: 但这解释不了品牌忠诚度。
cues.en: but that doesn't explain brand loyalty.

cues.zh: 大多数吸烟者会一直坚持抽那个让他们上瘾的品牌，直到它要了他们的命。
cues.en: Most smokers will stick with the brand that got them hooked until it kills them.

cues.zh: 那不是成瘾，那是另一回事。
cues.en: That's not addiction, that's something else.

cues.zh: 那是肠道里发生的一些混乱。
cues.en: That's some confusion that's happening in the gut.

cues.en: Let's switch for a minute and talk about computer programs, a completely different topic.

cues.en: Computer programs are the most complicated things humans make.

cues.zh: 除此之外，我们造不出任何东西能像程序这般复杂。
cues.en: We don't make anything else which is as complicated as programs.

cues.zh: 或函数等等，它们必须以极其
cues.en: or functions or other things, and they all have to work together in a way which is amazingly

cues.en: complicated.

cues.zh: 我们所做的一切，没有比软件更复杂的了。
cues.en: There's nothing we do that's more complicated than software.

cues.zh: 你可能会举出一些非常复杂的系统，比如飞机就非常复杂，
cues.en: You could point at systems which are very complicated, like an airplane is very complicated,

cues.zh: 没错，但飞机中最复杂的部件是软件。
cues.en: and that's true, but the most complicated component in an airplane is the software.

cues.en: That's true of all systems today.

cues.zh: 软件很复杂。
cues.en: Software is complicated.

cues.en: that programming is just too difficult and we should write programs that can write better

cues.en: programs than we can, because people are just not very good at this.

cues.en: Once we can get the program to do that, we can then tell the programs "make a program

cues.zh: ”，然后我们一直这么做，直到它们成为我们的霸主。
cues.en: that's better than you," and we keep doing that until they become our overlords.

cues.en: That didn't happen.

cues.zh: 人工智能失败了。
cues.en: Artificial intelligence failed.

cues.en: Artificial intelligence has done a lot of amazing things -- it can play grand master

cues.en: chess and a pretty good game of Jeopardy now -- but you can't give a set of requirements

cues.en: and custom router views to a computer and have it write the program for you.

cues.zh: 它做不到这一点。
cues.en: It can't do that.

cues.zh: 我们仍然在手工编写程序。
cues.en: We're still writing programs by hand.

cues.zh: 在技术思维的演进方面，我们取得的进展极其微小，
cues.en: We've made extremely small progress in the evolution of technological thinking around

cues.zh: 尤其是在编程领域。
cues.en: programming.

cues.zh: 我们最强大的工具就是编程语言。
cues.en: The most powerful tool we have is the programming language.

cues.zh: 它是我们与计算机之间的合作关系，计算机承担一部分工作，
cues.en: That is a partnership between us and the computer where it's doing some of the work and we're

cues.en: doing some of the work.

cues.en: The programming language allows us to work at a higher level of abstraction, which allows

cues.zh: 更高效，但本质上仍然是手工活儿。
cues.en: us to be more productive, but still it's basically handmade stuff.

cues.zh: 思考问题的方式。
cues.en: we think about things.

cues.en: Sometimes that's a really good thing if the programming language helps us to organize

cues.zh: 事物，但这也可能给我们造成盲区。
cues.en: things well, but that can also create blind spots in us.

cues.zh: 递归是多么宝贵的工具。
cues.en: of what a valuable tool recursion is.

cues.zh: 或者如果你的语言没有闭包，你就意识不到闭包
cues.en: Or if you have a language that doesn't have closures, you're not aware of what a valuable

cues.zh: 是多么宝贵的工具。
cues.en: tool closures are.

cues.zh: 所以，编程语言既帮我们也害我们。
cues.en: So, programming languages work for us and against us.

cues.en: The thing that makes programming so difficult is that it has to be perfect.

cues.zh: 一个程序必须在每个细节上都绝对完美，能应对所有可能的输入和
cues.en: A program has to be absolutely perfect in every detail for all possible inputs and all

cues.en: possible uses, even including uses which were not anticipated in the design of the program.

cues.zh: 如果程序里发现任何缺陷，计算机就可以在最糟糕的时候做出最糟糕的事，
cues.en: If any flaw is found in the program, the computer has license to do the worst possible thing

cues.zh: 而这不是计算机的错。
cues.en: at the worst possible time, and it is not the computer's fault.

cues.en: Whose fault is it?
